memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'For seven days present a food offering to the LORD. And on the
seventh day hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work'"
- Lev 23:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The festival did not last a moment; it lasted a week. Seven full days
of offerings, bookended by sacred assemblies. God was not interested
in a quick religious gesture followed by business as usual.

There is wisdom here about how change actually happens in us. A single
emotional moment rarely transforms a life. Sustained attention does.
Israel spent a whole week with the same truth in front of them: we were
slaves, and God brought us out.

Dear friend, we often want spiritual growth to arrive suddenly. One
powerful sermon, one moving worship night, one decisive prayer. Those
moments are real and God uses them. But the deep work usually happens
through repetition over time.

Paul told Timothy to be diligent in these matters, to give himself
wholly to them, so that everyone would see his progress (1 Tim 4:15).
Progress, not instant arrival. The writer to the Hebrews speaks of
those who by constant use have trained themselves to distinguish good
from evil (Heb 5:14).

Do not despise slow growth. The week-long festival taught Israel that
some truths need time to sink in.

Give God more than a moment this week.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I expecting instant change where God is asking for steady
   faithfulness?
2. What truth do I need to sit with for more than a moment?
3. Where have I given up too early on a spiritual habit?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, give me patience with the slow work You are doing in me. Help me
to keep showing up faithfully rather than chasing only the dramatic.
Amen.
